A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPI task, datasets, and TriMPI framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, efficiency measurements, policy-override and policy-referral results, and catastrophic-forgetting experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds policy-in-context evaluation, WildGuardTest results, and qualitative and quantitative error analyses.

M1.justification: The VM-CPT, CoT SFT, and PolicyRollout training stages, objectives, and rollout procedure are unchanged. Restoring policies during inference in the new experiment is an additional evaluation condition, not a revision of the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds WildGuardTest harmful-response classification in Appendix H and tests trained models with their original policies restored in-context in Section 5.4. ClevrPolicy-T/M, GTAPolicy, MMMU-Pro, MMLU-Pro, and the MPI training-data coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding existing experiments. The added evaluations reuse existing reference methods, including pretrained Qwen2.5-VL-7B, CoT SFT, and CoT SFT + GRPO; they introduce no new baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate trained Qwen2.5-VL-7B with policies restored in-context, measure harmfulness-classification accuracy, and compare generated Condition-ID frequencies against synthesized Gold CoT responses. These supplement the evaluation; previously reported splits, training budgets, model configurations, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 5.4–5.6 and Appendices H and M add a policy-restoration control, safety-retention testing, failures of the proposed model, and quantitative branching-error analysis. Together these substantially expand the robustness and diagnostic evidence beyond v1’s retained ablations and successful qualitative comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new Condition-ID distributions and discussion of variation across policy settings do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Matched existing results are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 4 and 10 and Figures 11–14. Table 10 reports average safety accuracy of 76.13% for TriMPI, 68.07% for CoT SFT, 66.92% for CoT SFT + GRPO, and 87.24% before training. Figure 14 reports branching discrepancies of 38.72, 39.74, and 7.07 for CoT SFT, CoT SFT + GRPO, and TriMPI; Section 5.6 appears to reverse the baseline-value order.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and training and reward equations remain unchanged, including appendix mathematics. The new branching analysis introduces an empirical diagnostic without adding a formal proposition, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same MPI task, two dataset contributions, TriMPI framework, and claims about performance, generalization, and forgetting. The headline 70.7% and 79.4% absolute gains are unchanged; new experiments provide additional support.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the restored-policy results as evidence that TriMPI’s advantage persists with policy access. It adds specific failure explanations involving perception, hallucinated branches, and misuse of tool history, and interprets branching-frequency agreement as better policy grounding. Appendix H adds a safety-consistency interpretation; the conclusion’s limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, model versions, data construction, and CoT generation instructions remain unchanged. The project page, supplementary-code statement, and future public-release commitment are retained; removing the duplicate release sentence from the abstract does not establish changed resource access.

R1.justification: v2 adds Han et al. (2024) for WildGuardTest. Existing discussions of prompt compression, deliberative alignment, rollout augmentation, and multimodal personalization retain their citations and positioning, including the renumbered additional-related-work appendix.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Sections 5.4 and 5.6 and Appendices H and M within the existing organization. It makes limited grammatical and cross-reference edits and changes the preprint header to an ICLR 2026 publication header. Most existing prose and narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with two new result tables and four error-analysis figures, including a six-panel distribution comparison. Figure 6 moves from a wrapped side figure to a centered display, and appendix figures are rearranged. Existing examples and policy illustrations are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new policy-restoration control, safety-retention test, and explicit failure analysis strengthen validation and make remaining limitations more visible than in v1. These are focused improvements to an otherwise stable paper. The apparent reversal of baseline-value order between Section 5.6 and Figure 14 introduces a small reporting defect, but does not outweigh the added evidence.
